Creativo@Work builds custom applications, storefronts, and learning platforms for small to
mid-sized companies — and modernizes the ones that outgrew their stack. Strategy before code,
performance measured after, no fluff in between.

---

## Services

### Custom application engineering
Auth, dashboards, APIs, and data models. Software with a real architecture, not a CMS bent into
the shape of one.

### Legacy platform modernization
Aging codebases moved onto current stacks incrementally, with the business still running while it
happens.

### Headless and composable front-ends
React and TypeScript against a decoupled CMS, so the editing experience and the front end stop
constraining each other. Includes headless WordPress.

### eCommerce engineering
WooCommerce storefronts that load fast, convert well, and scale with the catalog instead of
fighting it.

### Learning platforms
LMS platforms with the cohort, certification, and reporting features your operation actually uses.

### AI feature integration
Retrieval over your own content, assisted workflows, and the evaluation work that tells you
whether it is actually helping.

### Cloud infrastructure and delivery
Pipelines, environments, monitoring, and the unglamorous operational work that keeps everything
quiet.

### Product and interface design
Interface design grounded in your audience and your goals, not in last quarter's component library
trends.

### Performance, SEO and analytics
Core Web Vitals, technical SEO, and instrumentation that reads what changed and why.

---

## Technology

TypeScript, React, headless CMS architecture, WordPress, headless WordPress, WooCommerce, cloud
infrastructure and CI/CD, AI and LLM feature integration, Core Web Vitals and technical SEO.

## About

**Designed to be different. Built to deliver.**

We stay small so the people who scope your project are the people who build it. No account layer,
no handoff between the brief and the code.

Most of our work starts with something that already exists — a platform that outgrew its stack, a
site nobody can edit without a developer, an internal tool held together by spreadsheets. We
modernize incrementally, in production, instead of proposing the year-long rewrite that never
ships.

Fewer projects at once, direct access to the people building, and a bias toward decisions you can
still reverse in eighteen months.

- **Studio:** Brooklyn, NY
- **Founded:** 2020
- **Team:** Small by design
- **Stack:** TypeScript · React · Headless

---

## Who we work with

Founders, marketing leads, and creative directors at small-to-midsize companies who need a partner
across strategy, design, build, and the long tail of optimization after launch.

## Frequently asked questions

Canonical page: https://creativoatwork.com/faq

### What does Creativo@Work do?

Creativo@Work is a web and platform development studio in Brooklyn, New York. We build custom web
applications, headless and composable front-ends, WooCommerce storefronts, and learning platforms
for small to mid-sized companies — and we modernize existing systems that have outgrown their
stack. Most engagements cover strategy, design, build, and the long tail of optimization after
launch, rather than a single phase handed off to someone else.

We deliberately stay small, so the people who scope a project are the people who write the code.
There is no account-management layer between your brief and the engineers building against it. In
practice that means fewer projects running at once, direct access to the people doing the work, and
architectural decisions you can still reverse eighteen months from now.

### Where is Creativo@Work located, and do you work with clients outside New York?

Our studio is at 195 Plymouth Street, Suite 5/5, Brooklyn, NY 11201, and we work with clients well
beyond New York. Being in New York matters for the clients who want to sit in a room together; it
does not limit who we take on. We run engagements remotely as a matter of course, and our client
work spans the United States, Europe, and Latin America.

Studio hours are Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 18:00 Eastern Time, and we work async-friendly across
time zones — written updates, recorded walkthroughs, and shared environments you can check on your
own schedule rather than meetings scheduled at inconvenient hours. If you are local to New York
City and prefer to meet in person, we are happy to.

### How much does a custom web application or website cost?

Cost depends on scope, and we quote a fixed price per project after a scoping conversation rather
than publishing a rate card that would not survive contact with your actual requirements. What
moves the number most is not page count but complexity:

- how many user roles and permissions the system has to enforce;
- whether you need payments, subscriptions, or billing;
- how much data has to migrate out of an existing system, and how clean it is;
- how many third-party services need integrating;
- whether a live platform has to keep running while it is being modernized.

A brochure site and a multi-tenant application with billing are different orders of magnitude. We
would rather tell you early that a piece of scope is expensive relative to its value than discover
it at invoice time, so scoping is where we spend real effort. Send us what you have — even a rough
brief — and we will come back with a scope and a number.

### How long does a typical project take?

Timelines are set during scoping and depend on the same factors that drive cost: integrations, data
migration, the number of user roles, and how much of an existing system has to keep running while
the new one is built. Rather than quote a generic number, we plan projects in increments that ship.
You see working software early and often, not a long silence followed by a single reveal at the
end.

For modernization work in particular, we sequence the plan so that value lands in production along
the way instead of at the very end — the riskiest thing you can do with a legacy platform is
disappear for a year. Two things reliably shorten a timeline: decisions made promptly, and one
person on your side empowered to make them.

### Can you modernize a legacy platform without rebuilding it from scratch?

Yes — incremental modernization is the core of what we do, and it is usually the right call. The
full rewrite is the most commonly proposed and most commonly failed approach to a legacy system: it
freezes the existing product, takes far longer than estimated, and asks the business to run on the
old platform while paying for a new one that has not shipped.

We work the other way. We move an aging codebase onto a current stack in stages, in production,
with the business still running while it happens. That typically means putting a modern front end
in front of the existing system, migrating one bounded piece at a time, and keeping the old and new
paths running side by side until the new one is proven. Each stage is independently useful, so the
project is worth something even if priorities change halfway through.

### What is headless WordPress, and is it right for our site?

Headless WordPress means keeping WordPress as the editing environment while the public site is
rendered by a separate front end — in our case React and TypeScript — which talks to WordPress over
an API. Your team keeps the editor it already knows; the front end is no longer constrained by
themes, plugin conflicts, or PHP rendering.

It is the right choice when the editorial experience and the front-end experience are pulling
against each other: when the site needs to be faster than the theme allows, when the design has
outgrown what a theme can express, or when the same content needs to feed a site, an app, and a
partner integration.

It is the wrong choice when a well-built conventional WordPress theme would do the job — going
headless adds a deployment pipeline and a second codebase to maintain. We will tell you which
situation you are in before you spend money on the more complex option.

### Do you build WooCommerce stores, and can WooCommerce handle a large catalog?

Yes, we build and rebuild WooCommerce storefronts, and WooCommerce handles large catalogs well when
it is engineered for it. Most slow WooCommerce stores are not slow because of WooCommerce; they are
slow because of accumulated plugins, unindexed database queries, uncached product pages, and images
shipped at full resolution. Those are engineering problems with engineering fixes.

Our commerce work focuses on the things that actually move revenue: catalog and search performance
as the number of products grows, checkout that does not lose people on mobile, correct handling of
variations and inventory, and Core Web Vitals measured on real devices rather than a lab score. We
are equally willing to tell you when a headless storefront in front of WooCommerce is worth the
added complexity and when it is not.

### Can you build a custom learning platform instead of using an off-the-shelf LMS?

Yes. We build learning management systems with the cohort, certification, and reporting features an
operation actually uses, and we have shipped course platforms for education clients. The honest
answer to build-versus-buy is that off-the-shelf platforms are excellent until your model diverges
from theirs. If you sell self-paced courses to individuals, an existing platform is usually the
cheaper path.

Custom becomes the better investment when your requirements do not fit the mold:

- cohort-based programs with enrollment windows;
- certification and accreditation tracking with an audit trail;
- institutional or B2B licensing with seat management;
- reporting your accreditor or client demands in a specific shape;
- integration with a CRM or student records system you already run.

We will say plainly which case you are in, including when the answer is that you do not need us to
build one.

### What does AI feature integration actually mean for a small or mid-sized company?

In practice it means three concrete things.

**Retrieval over your own content**, so people can ask questions in plain language and get answers
grounded in your documents rather than invented ones. **Assisted workflows**, where a step that used
to require reading and re-keying — triage, summarizing, drafting a first pass, extracting structured
data from documents — gets done faster with a person still reviewing it. And **the evaluation work**
that tells you whether either is actually helping.

That last part is the one most often skipped and the reason most AI features quietly underperform.
Without a test set and a measurement, nobody can tell the difference between a feature that works
and one that produces confident, plausible, wrong output. We build the evaluation alongside the
feature. We are also comfortable advising against it: if the underlying process is not worth
automating, adding a language model does not change that.

### Do you maintain and support what you build after launch?

Yes. Launch is a milestone, not the end of the engagement, and we keep running most of what we
build. Ongoing work covers dependency and security updates, monitoring and uptime, performance and
Core Web Vitals as content and traffic grow, analytics and instrumentation that show what changed
and why, and the steady stream of small improvements that a live product generates.

We also hand over cleanly. You own your code and your infrastructure, and we document what we build
so another team could pick it up — retaining us should be a choice you keep making because the work
is good, not a position you are locked into by an undocumented codebase only we understand.
